discovery: Quantum simulation of strongly correlated many-body physics with ultracold atoms in optical lattices

nominees.name: Immanuel Bloch
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Quantum Optics and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Germany

nominees.name: Peter Zoller
nominees.affiliation: University of Innsbruck and IQOQI, Austrian Academy of Sciences, Austria

subfield: Atomic, molecular and optical physics / quantum simulation
motivation: Zoller and co-workers showed theoretically in 1998 that cold atoms in optical lattices realize the Bose-Hubbard model with tunable parameters. In 2002 Greiner and Bloch observed the quantum phase transition from a superfluid to a Mott insulator, turning a textbook condensed-matter model into a clean, quantitatively controlled experiment. The field then grew into quantum simulation. Bloch and Greiner built quantum gas microscopes that image and address single atoms at single lattice sites. With them they observed Mott shells, antiferromagnetic order and string correlations in the Fermi-Hubbard model, many-body localization and entanglement entropy. Zoller's proposals, including lattice gauge theories and Rydberg-mediated interactions, defined much of the agenda. Together their work made analog quantum simulation a precise tool for problems beyond classical computation, and it now drives research across atomic, condensed-matter and quantum-information physics.
